title: Optimal truthful pricing from one sample
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: Determine the best prior-independent expected revenue ratio ρ_MHR attainable by a randomized posted price based on one independent sample, for the continuous MHR class specified below.
definitions: The distribution class consists of absolutely continuous laws F on [0,∞), with density f, finite positive mean and 0<R*(F)<∞, for which h(x)=f(x)/(1−F(x)) admits a nondecreasing version on {x:F(x)<1}. Atoms are excluded in this explicit continuous variant. Draw sample S and buyer value V independently from F. A pricing rule is any measurable stochastic kernel K from S to a finite nonnegative price P, using private randomness independent of V. It knows neither F nor any other sample, support bound, moment or scale. The buyer sees P and buys iff V≥P, paying P on purchase and zero otherwise. This is a truthful take-it-or-leave-it offer. The monopoly benchmark is R*(F)=sup_{p≥0}p Pr_F[V≥p]. Define ρ_MHR=sup_K inf_F E[P 1[V≥P]]/R*(F), where K is fixed before F is chosen. No computational restriction or scale-invariance assumption is imposed on K.
answer_criterion: Supply a real approximation a to the defined optimal constant and a complete Lean-checked proof of absolute error at most 1/100. A certified interval of width at most 1/50 qualifies via its midpoint. Exact identification is welcome but not required; an infimum or supremum need not be attained. The cited interval [0.644,0.648] is already narrower than this benchmark tolerance: the missing work for this numerical target is certification of suitable bounds, not discovery of a new 0.01-accurate estimate. The exact optimum remains a different, stronger question.
context:
Hartline’s survey reports a narrow interval for truthful randomized sample pricing and distinguishes the substantially different non-revelation mechanism class.

The reported interval contains 0.646 with error at most 0.002. Consequently the default numerical tolerance does not represent a presently unresolved mathematical accuracy target; no Lean certificate is claimed here.
